BiblicalUsage: Serug is a patriarch of the line from Shem to Abraham: Reu lived two and thirty years, and begat Serug, and Serug lived after he begat Nahor two hundred years. The chronicler carries the same line — Serug, Nahor, Terah — down to Abraham.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Serug's place is the quiet middle of the promise: a father in the chain, named because the chain has no missing piece.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
